_comment: ONE IMPOUNDMENT PER THREE CHUNKS, DERIVED RATHER THAN PICKED (rewritten 2026-08-23).
This shipped as count 4 per chunk over 5-11 wide heaps. The coverage arithmetic was right and the
result still read as a field of cupcakes with a drum on every summit - a screenshot found what the
census could not. The reference is Moab and Church Rock: ONE enormous engineered pile with a decant
pond on it, not dozens of small mounds.
So: radius 9-12 for a footprint near pi*10.5^2 = 346 columns, at one attempt per 3 chunks. That is
346 / (3 * 256) = 0.45x coverage against the old 0.77x, while each pile is roughly seven times the
area of an old one. Fewer, far bigger, and there is open stained ground between them again - which
the biome needs, because it is in the encroachment tag precisely so grass is CONTESTED on open
THE RADIUS CEILING IS AN ENGINE LIMIT. ChunkStatus.FEATURES has blockStateWriteRadius(1), so a
feature may only write to its own chunk and the eight around it - 16 blocks from the origin in the
worst case. The longest lobe plus the stain ring is 12 * 1.21 + 1 = 15.5, so radius 12 is the most
this can be. A draft of this rewrite used 16 and would have logged an ERROR per rejected block and
sheared every pile along a chunk line.
For comparison the other scatters: rubble_pile 6 x ~21 = 0.49x, mechanical_waste_pile 2.
